{{Quote|The Force is within everything.''"<br />"''But here and now, in this cantina, in the trenches of Hoth, or falling toward some nameless moon of Endor&mdash;the Force binds it ''all''.|Dice Ibegon and Lak Sivrak|<ref name="One Last Night" />}}
'''Dice Ibegon''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Lamproid/Legends|Lamproid]], a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], and the lover of [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]]. A native of the harsh jungle [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Florn/Legends|Florn]], Ibegon was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] and was rumored to have the ability to [[Time travel/Legends|shift]] through [[Time/Legends|time]]. She became a recruiter for the Rebel Alliance during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], eventually winding up in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. There, she met a [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] outlaw, Lak Sivrak, and the two fell immediately in love. Ibegon persuaded Sivrak to join the Alliance, and they both served for a year between [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].

Ibegon fought alongside Sivrak in the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], though they were separated and she was fatally wounded by falling debris. She had time for several last words to Sivrak, telling him to continue his fight against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], before she [[Death/Legends|died]]. The Force would allow the two lovers to meet each other again as they relived past experiences, until Sivrak was himself killed at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Ibegon and Sivrak became [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghosts]], and they stayed on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] for eternity.

==Biography==
===Rebel===
Dice Ibegon was a [[Lamproid/Legends|Florn Lamproid]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Florn/Legends|Florn]]<ref name="One Last Night" /> in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. Like all Florn Lamproids,<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> Ibegon was a predator, with rows of sharp teeth and a poison stinger; these were put to good use on Florn, a wild jungle world inhabited by a plethora of vicious predators. Ibegon was a talented hunter, and the hunt held great significance for her.<ref name="One Last Night" /> A large amount of Florn Lamproids were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]];<ref name="NEGAS" /> Ibegon was among these, and she was believed to have possessed a peculiar [[Time/Legends|time]]-[[Time travel/Legends|shifting]] attunement with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="CCG" /> which allowed her to relive past moments while retaining her memories of the first time the events took place. This ability could also be practiced after Ibegon's [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="One Last Night" /> Florn Lamproids as a [[Species/Legends|species]] were sympathetic to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> and Ibegon herself eventually joined the Rebellion, acting as a recruiter on remote [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] worlds.<ref name="One Last Night" />

===Love===
{{Quote|We ''are'' alike, as you have always known. The hunter and the killer know the sick and diseased must be culled from the herd&mdash;and the Empire is rotten with corruption. That is why you must leave me, to continue our fight until its end.|Ibegon's dying words|<ref name="One Last Night" />}}
She eventually found her way to the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], where she occasionally frequented the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley cantina]],<ref name="One Last Night" /> drinking [[Blood/Legends|blood]] mixes of questionable origin.<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> She eventually met [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]]&mdash;known to most as only Sivrak&mdash;a secretive [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] Wolfman fugitive who had slain a group of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] troops. Although he and Ibegon had markedly different body structures, Sivrak found the Lamproid extremely attractive, and Ibegon made efforts to seduce him, buying the Shistavanen a drink and inviting him to sit with her. The two found that they had much in common: they were both by nature predators, and they both hated the Empire. Ibegon eventually told Sivrak about the Force&mdash;how it bound all life together&mdash;and that she was a member of the Rebel Alliance. Sivrak told her of his own Rebel sympathies, though Ibegon knew that this was just a ruse to make him appear a more suitable romantic companion for the Lamproid. She did not care: her role was to recruit suitable candidates to the Rebellion, and Sivrak was certainly a suitable candidate. She also enjoyed his company immensely, and the two eventually shared a "predator's kiss."<ref name="One Last Night" /> At some point, the two left each other for a time, with a [[Pacithhip/Legends|Pacithhip]] named [[Ketwol/Legends|Ketwol]] taking Sivrak's vacant seat.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:Florn_Lamproid_front_view.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dice Ibegon]]
During Ibegon and Sivrak's time at the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], an elderly man entered the building, accompanied by a younger man and a [[C-3PO/Legends|golden protocol droid]]. The younger man, named [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], got into an argument with an [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] thug named [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]]; the older [[Human/Legends|Human]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], was eventually forced to interject and used his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to slice off one of the Aqualish's arm. The spectacle grabbed everyone's attention initially, though most went back to their conversations after several moments;<ref name="ANH" /> Sivrak and Ibegon did not, as they knew that authorities would arrive to investigate, and Sivrak would be executed by the Empire if any [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] recognized him.<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

The two left the cantina forever, taking up residence together. They spent many nights discussing the Rebellion, and grew deeply in love.<ref name="EGTC" /> Although he had initially only claimed allegiance to the Rebels to make himself seem more attractive to Ibegon, Sivrak eventually did become loyal to the Rebellion's cause and for which it stood.<ref name="One Last Night" /> In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Ibegon and Sivrak formally joined the Alliance,<ref name="EGTC" /> becoming soldiers on the front lines. They were stationed at the Rebels' secret [[Echo Base/Legends|base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]],<ref name="One Last Night" /> though a year after they became soldiers, the Empire learned of the Rebel presence on Hoth and attacked the ice world.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Ibegon and Sivrak acted as [[Alliance Army/Legends|infantry]], fighting in the trenches against the Imperial ground troops and [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-ATs]] while Echo Base was evacuated and Rebel [[Transport/Legends|transports]] fled Hoth.<ref name="One Last Night" />

The two lovers were eventually separated, and Ibegon was grievously wounded when a large piece of shrapnel deeply punctured her thorax, causing Ibegon to lose a large amount of her purple blood. Sivrak located her, though by that point she had bled too much to have any chance of survival. Ibegon told Sivrak to continue his fight against the Empire, and to believe in the Force, before finally passing away. Sivrak had heard stories of how the Empire used body parts of Rebel corpses for research purposes, and, not wanting his lover's memory to be insulted, he used a powerful [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] to disintegrate her snakelike body. Ibegon eventually became a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]].<ref name="One Last Night" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Tell me what is happening.''"<br />"''Only that which has happened.|Lak Sivrak and Dice Ibegon, reliving their first encounter|<ref name="One Last Night" />}}
Sivrak did continue to serve with the Rebels, participating in many battles up until the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> Sivrak never forgot his deceased lover, and, a year after her death, he still mourned her and found life without her to be pointless and mundane. While piloting an [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] against Imperial forces at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], Sivrak relived the time he first met Ibegon at Mos Eisley years before. However, he retained his previous recollection of events, and knew what would happen to him and others around him. Ibegon and Sivrak spoke with each other: much of their dialog was the same as had originally occurred, though some of it was different. They each shared their knowledge of what was to transpire to the cantina's other patrons, though Sivrak eventually became extremely confused, and questioned Ibegon on what was actually happening&mdash;he was unsure if it was somehow connected to the Force, or if it was merely a hallucination. The reliving of the memory was cut short, as Sivrak's consciousness returned to what was transpiring in real-time at Endor, where he was being pursued by a group of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]].<ref name="One Last Night" />

Several minutes later, Sivrak returned to the time Ibegon was killed on Hoth, though events there transpired mostly as they had done originally. The next memory he relived was not one he had ever actually lived through; he and Ibegon were in [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun's]] cantina, a year after her death, speaking about the demise of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] lord [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. This baffled Sivrak, though he was beginning to understand that the Force was allowing him and Ibegon to wade through time. The memory merged itself with the first memory that had been relived, when Ibegon and Sivrak had first met. Sivrak's consciousness eventually returned to Endor, where his badly-damaged [[Starship/Legends|ship]] crashed into the [[Moon/Legends|moon's]] surface, and he was killed. Ibegon joined her lover as a Force ghost, watching over the Rebels and their [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] allies as they celebrated their victory over the Empire. The two stayed on Endor as Force ghosts for all eternity.<ref name="One Last Night" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Dice_Ibegon_action_figure.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Dice Ibegon]]
{{Quote|The Force binds all, if you would believe in it.|Dice Ibegon|<ref name="One Last Night" />}}
Dice Ibegon believed in the Force, that it would guide her path and that it bound all things. Because of her time-shifting connection to the Force, Ibegon often knew what would happen before it did, giving her an aura of mystery. She was very tough and resilient, though; she had to be in order to survive on her harsh [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Much of her life revolved around hunting, and she saw herself and Sivrak as hunters preying on a corrupt and unhealthy Empire. Ibegon hated that the Empire was mired with corruption, and saw it as her duty to be part of the movement to stop it.<ref name="One Last Night" />

Ibegon had a mild proficiency for the Force, and many believed she had the ability to travel through time in some form.<ref name="CCG" /> She was able to haunt the dreams of Lak Sivrak even after her death,<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> taking him to important moments in their lives. After Sivrak's death, the two lovers stayed on Endor as Force ghosts for eternity.<ref name="One Last Night" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ibegon first appeared was as a background character in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where she sat next to Lak Sivrak in the cantina scene.<ref name="SW.com">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> After the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Original Trilogy Special Edition]] was released in [[1997]], Sivrak's on-screen role was replaced by Ketwol, though the wolfman can still be seen briefly in the background.<ref name="ANH" /> Ibegon's puppet was nicknamed "Snake Head" by the production crew of ''A New Hope'' because of its appearance, and was eventually given the proper name of "Nake."<ref name="SW.com" /> This name was disregarded by [[Judith Reeves-Stevens|Judith]] and [[Garfield Reeves-Stevens]] in their short story, ''[[One Last Night in the Mos Eisley Cantina: The Tale of the Wolfman and the Lamproid]]'', which identified the character as Dice Ibegon. Since ''One Last Night&hellip;'', which was printed in ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'', Ibegon has only been mentioned in the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]], the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'', and Lak Sivrak's entry in ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', though she also appeared briefly in the non-[[canon]] comic, "[[The Emperor's Court]]."

Since the Dice Ibegon prop was a hand puppet, she is only shown from the neck upwards in the movie. Her full anatomy was revealed in a 2009 [[Hasbro]] action figure, as part of a pack-in with [[Trinto Duaba/Legends|Trinto Duaba]].
